Title: 

Reform had already pledged to ban foreign students from taxpayer-funded student loan

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Reform had already pledged to ban foreign students from taxpayer-funded student loan

BookmarkCommentsGo to commentsBookmark popoverRemoved from bookmarks

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

International graduates owing student loan debts would face entry bans to the UK unless they settle their balances under new proposals put forward by Reform UK.

The party further stated that visas held by foreign students currently residing in the UK would be cancelled if they fall behind on their repayments.

According to Reform’s figures, European Union citizens residing overseas have failed to pay approximately £360 million over the past 12 months.

Party data indicates that out of 103,400 EU citizens abroad earning above the repayment threshold, 43,700 (42%) made no single repayment.

Reform claims that total unrecovered debts from overseas students could eventually exceed £1.5 billion.

At present, around 172,000 EU students hold £6.23 billion in outstanding UK loans.

Criticising previous administrations, Reform’s home affairs spokesman Zia Yusuf said: "Tory and Labour governments have helped foreign nationals scam British taxpayers.

"British people will rightly be furious to learn foreign students have come here using loans funded by British taxpayers, only to flee.

"This scam has already cost the British taxpayer £360 million.

"No more taxpayer-funded loans for foreign students, and those failing to make the repayments will be banned from entering Britain.

"We will stand up for British people."

The political party previously committed to completely barring non-UK students from receiving state-backed student finance, proposing instead to reallocate those funds towards establishing 600,000 apprenticeships.

While standard international students are not eligible for public loans, EU citizens who secured settled status following Brexit retain eligibility.
